answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering works after the fact. Each agent's request timing, tool sequences, and error patterns form an ivory signature that the detector clusters; identities whose signatures exceed a similarity threshold are flagged as one operator. The attacker must then generate genuinely distinct behavior per clone, paying compute and latency to vary each profile against an atlas of known clusters. Residual risk rises on the horizon as attackers learn the detector, so threshold tuning stays ongoing.
